questions.text: The lower degree of cohesion is kind of:
questions.solution:
Coincidental cohesion (elements grouped for no meaningful reason) is the lowest/worst level. Logical, procedural and communicational are higher.

Answer: Coincidental Cohesion

questions.text: In unit testing of a module, it is found that for a set of test data, at the maximum 90% of the code alone were tested with the probability of success 0.9. The reliability of module is
questions.solution:
Only 90% of the code was exercised, and that part succeeded with probability 0.9. The untested 10% gives no guarantee, so reliability is at most 0.9 [latex]\times[/latex] 0.9 = 0.81.

Answer: At most 0.81

questions.text:
In a particular program, it is found that 1% of the code account for 50% of the execution time. To code a program in C++, it takes 100 man-days. Coding in assembly language is 10 times harder than coding in C++, but runs 5 times faster. Converting an existing C++ program into an assembly language program is 4 times faster.
To completely write the program in C++ and rewrite the 1% code in assembly language, if a project team needs 13 days, the team consist of
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Writing the whole program in C++: 100 man-days.
- Writing 1% in assembly from scratch would take 0.01 [latex]\times[/latex] 100 [latex]\times[/latex] 10 = 10 man-days; converting is 4 times faster: 2.5 man-days.

Total = 102.5 man-days. In 13 days: 102.5 / 13 [latex]\approx[/latex] 7.9 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 programmers.

Answer: 8 programmers

questions.text: In the context of modular software design, which one of the following combinations is desirable?
questions.solution:
Good modular design wants each module to do one focused job (high cohesion) and depend little on other modules (low coupling).

Answer: High cohesion and low coupling
